Reason: The yellow arrow points to a widened left superior mediastinum, which, combined with mild cardiomegaly and hypoxaemia, is characteristic of a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC) draining into the left atrium causing a right-to-left shunt; this specific anatomical variant explains the symptoms better than heart failure or mass effect given the "mild" nature of findings and lack of frank edema. *(guided by t000002)*
